prerequisites: Capacity to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge on: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics and optimization.
Understanding and mastery of basic concepts regarding general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves and electromagnetism and their application to solving engineering problems.
Basic knowledge about the use and programming of computers, operating systems, databases and software with application in engineering.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the fundamentals of electronics.
Acquire and develop fundamental knowledge of electronics in the field of Engineering.
Coherently apply basic knowledge of electronics to various fields of action, proposing the most suitable solutions.
Work with the knowledge inherent to the subject for the correct application of electronic devices, using specific vocabulary and terminology and respecting established deadlines.
Work in a team, adopting a flexible attitude towards colleagues' proposals.
Adopt a spirit of improvement towards learning and applications of the subject.

teaching_methods: Lectures (M), used to present the topics established in the subject's program.
Classroom Practices (PA), used as a complement to lectures, developing practical exercises and questions; work will be done individually and in small groups.
Laboratory Practices (PL) will be the practical complement to the subject.
assessment_rules: The final grade is the sum of the written exam (80%) and laboratory work (20%). To pass, a minimum of 50% is required in both the written exam and the laboratory component, plus a minimum of 40% in each part of the written exam (theory and exercises). If these minimums are not met, the maximum final grade will be 4 out of 10. To renounce the ordinary call, students simply do not attend the written exam; approved laboratory or written exam scores are retained for the extraordinary call. In the extraordinary call, students who passed the lab will take a written exam, while those who did not pass the lab will take both a written and a practical exam, with the same minimum score requirements applying.
